figures.alt_text: Stepwise permission diagram with a top shared finite boundary screen of b0 through b5 bits feeding a left licensed-use lane and a right blocked-ontology lane, each labeled with the audit control that supports or blocks the reading.
figures.caption: Boundary use versus boundary ontology rendered as a stepwise permission diagram for the no-self-evidence claim. Step 1 shows the shared finite b0-b5 bitstream as the only evidenced object; Step 2 licenses reading those same bits through admissible QRF sector labels for prediction, policy selection, and model comparison when the equal-distribution audit passes; Step 3 blocks treating any chosen sector frame as a real self/world boundary because the perturbation control fails. Color encodes the licensed and blocked lanes, while the legend names the two verdicts, keeping the figure a finite software audit and not empirical, neural, clinical, practice-efficacy, or physical qFEP evidence.
figures.visual_encoding: Stepwise schematic; a top source box and b0-b5 bit cells encode the shared finite boundary screen, arrows encode the two possible readings, numbered badges and large rounded boxes encode licensed use versus blocked ontology, teal and amber borders encode pass and blocked verdicts, italic audit strips encode the bound validator flags, and the legend maps each verdict color.

figures.alt_text: Line chart with metacognitive access on the horizontal axis and the separation prior's net value as delta free energy on the vertical axis; one line is drawn per prior precision, the bolded weakest-precision line begins in the keep band and falls into the prune band at a dashed crossing marker, and the stronger precision lines stay in the prune band throughout.
figures.caption: Life-cycle of the separation prior's net value, the change in free energy when the prior is removed, against metacognitive access, drawn as one line per prior precision rather than a mean. The bolded arc is the precision whose net value actually crosses keep to prune (the weakest admissible precision for the current sweep); it starts positive in the shaded keep region and falls into the shaded prune region as access rises, while the fainter stronger-precision lines stay in the prune region throughout. The dashed marker locates the useful-to-dispensable crossing, and the figure is a finite software sweep, not a developmental, neural, contemplative, or clinical claim.
figures.visual_encoding: Single-panel line chart; one line per prior precision encodes delta free energy versus metacognitive access on the axes, the bolded line marks the precision whose net value crosses zero, shaded keep and prune bands encode the sign of net value, a dashed vertical line marks the crossing access, and the legend names each precision line.

figures.alt_text: Bar chart of minimum bipartition negativity for each entanglement fixture, where the GHZ, W, and qutrit bars rise above zero while the separable product control bars sit at zero negativity along the value axis.
figures.caption: Minimum bipartition negativity per fixture for the multipartite and higher-dimensional entanglement witness suite. Bars encode the smallest single-subsystem-versus-rest negativity for each GHZ, W, and qutrit fixture, colored to separate entangled fixtures that are detected on every cut from the separable product false-positive controls that must stay at zero negativity; the legend maps the two colors and the figure is a finite PPT/negativity witness over fixed states, not a genuine-multipartite-entanglement certificate and not empirical, neural, or physical qFEP evidence.
figures.visual_encoding: Single-panel bar chart; the bar height encodes minimum bipartition negativity per fixture, teal versus amber bar color encodes entangled fixtures versus separable false-positive controls, a zero reference line marks the control level, and the legend maps each color to a fixture class.

figures.alt_text: Two-panel bar chart where the left panel axis shows maximum bond dimension per fixture (entangled at two, product at one) and the right panel axis shows bond-one truncation error that is positive for entangled fixtures and zero for product fixtures.
figures.caption: Tensor-network matrix-product-state benchmark shown as two panels. Panel A bars encode the maximum bond dimension per fixture, with entangled GHZ and W states staying at bond two and product states at bond one as the screen grows, demonstrating tractability beyond exact state-vector enumeration; Panel B bars encode the bond-one truncation error, which is positive on entangled fixtures and zero on products, the discriminating control. The figure is a finite exact-MPS benchmark over toy states, not a large-scale many-body simulation and not empirical evidence.
figures.visual_encoding: Two-panel bar chart; Panel A bar height encodes maximum bond dimension with color separating entangled and product fixtures, Panel B bar height encodes bond-one truncation error with color separating lossy entangled bars from lossless product bars, and each panel legend maps the colors to fixture classes.

figures.alt_text: Grouped bar chart with one pair of bars per coupling strength, where the final trace-distance bar drops far below the initial bar for the weak and strong couplings but equals the initial bar for the zero-coupling control along the distance axis.
figures.caption: Collision-model thermalization surrogate shown as grouped bars of the trace distance from the system qubit to the fixed ancilla, initial versus final, for each coupling strength. The weak and strong partial-SWAP couplings collapse the final distance toward zero while the zero-coupling control leaves the final distance equal to the initial value, the discriminating control; the legend maps the initial and final bars. The figure is a finite deterministic collision surrogate, not a physical heat bath or thermodynamic measurement and not empirical evidence.
figures.visual_encoding: Single-panel grouped bar chart; paired bar heights encode the initial and final trace distance to the ancilla per coupling on the value axis, color separates the initial from the final bar, and the legend names both.

figures.alt_text: Matrix with one row per cycle length and one column per behavior, where cells are colored and labeled feasible or infeasible, showing odd-cycle rows infeasible at the anti-correlation and quantum columns while even-cycle rows and the uncorrelated column stay feasible.
figures.caption: n-cycle contextuality scenario library shown as a feasibility matrix. Rows are cycle lengths labeled odd or even and two-colorable or frustrated, columns are the perfect anti-correlation, quantum, and uncorrelated behaviors, and each colored cell encodes whether the noncontextual-polytope linear program is feasible (a noncontextual model exists) or infeasible (contextual). Odd cycles including the five-cycle pentagon are contextual while even cycles are not, cross-checked against graph two-colorability; the matrix records measured LP feasibility, not an asserted optimal violation, and is not empirical evidence.
figures.visual_encoding: Single-panel categorical matrix; rows encode cycle length and parity, columns encode the three behaviors, two-color cell fill and cell text encode feasible versus infeasible LP verdicts, and the legend maps the colors to noncontextual versus contextual.
